data: Tesla's GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders was about $12.56 billion ($12,556 million) in fiscal 2022 and about $7.09 billion ($7,091 million) in fiscal 2024. That is a decline of roughly $5.47 billion, or about 43.5% over the two years. Fiscal 2024's figure was itself boosted by a one-time non-cash tax benefit of about $5.9 billion that Tesla recorded in fiscal 2023 from releasing a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, which continued to affect comparisons. Measured on total net income including noncontrolling interests, the figures are about $12.59 billion for 2022 and $7.15 billion for 2024, which also works out to a drop of roughly 43%. The main causes were lower vehicle prices, a smaller automotive gross margin and higher operating expenses.
